6.0.s.en: 1. A prophecy against the mountains of Israel:

6.0.0.en: 1 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 “Son of man, set thy face toward the mountains of Israel, and prophesy unto them, 3 And say, Ye mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD; Thus saith the Lord GOD to the mountains, and to the hills, to the valleys, and to the lowlands; Behold, I, even I, will bring a sword upon you, and I will destroy your high places. 4 And your altars shall be desolate, and your sun images shall be broken: and I will cast down your slain men before your idols. 5 And I will lay the dead carcases of the children of Israel before their idols; and I will scatter your bones round about your altars. 6 In all your dwellingplaces the cities shall be laid waste, and the high places shall be desolate; that your altars may be laid waste and made desolate, and your idols may be broken and cease, and your sun images may be cut down, and your works may be abolished. 7 And the slain shall fall in the midst of you, and ye shall know that I am the LORD.

6.0.1.en: The Jews took from the pagans their worship of idols on the mountains, hills, rivers and valleys. Therefore the Lord asked the prophet Ezekiel to direct his gaze toward the mountains of Israel, which had been defiled by pagan worship, and to prophesy against them. He looks like a judge who looks toward the accused in order to pass sentence on him face to face, to shake his foundations and destroy them.

6.0.2.en: Mountains have a symbolic meaning in the Holy Bible. For “the earth” often signifies in the Holy Bible the soul that has descended to earthly thought, so that the earthly body with its lusts has taken it captive and bound it to material things, whereas “the mountains” often signify in the Holy Bible souls lifted above earthly things to dwell with Him in the heavenly places, a holy, heavenly Church. For this reason God often ascribes the mountain to Himself and calls it “his holy mountain” (Ps 2:6), (Ps 99:9; Isa 65:11, 25; Joel 2:1; Obad 16), and the Holy Bible also calls it “Jerusalem, thy holy mountain” (Dan 9:16; Isa 66:20), “Zion my holy mountain” (Joel 3:17).

6.0.3.en: The two angels asked Lot to flee to the mountain lest he perish (Gen 9:17), as though asking him to rise above temporal things lest they ensnare him in their whirlpool. And the psalmist longed to dwell in the holy hill of the Lord (Ps 15:1), that is, for his heart to be lifted up on high, where it meets God who dwells in the heights and who answers him (Ps 30:4).

6.0.4.en: The soul that becomes a holy mountain becomes like Mount Horeb, where the Lord comes to it, not to give it His Law engraved on stones as to Moses, but to engrave His commandment on its heart by the Holy Spirit. The Lord sits in it as He sat on the mount to teach the multitudes with His words, drawing them to Himself with authority (Mt 5). It becomes like the mount of temptation, on which the Lord Himself ascends to lead the spiritual battle against Satan, shattering his authority, so that the soul gains the ability to overcome and the angels come to minister to it. It becomes like Mount Tabor, where the soul enjoys fellowship with the men of the Old Testament (Moses and Elijah) and the men of the New Testament (Peter, James and John) in the presence of the Lord Christ Himself, who overshadows it with His bright cloud and reveals His radiance to it within. It becomes like the Mount of Olives, where the Lord sits in it weeping over His fallen children who killed the prophets and stoned His messengers, so that it becomes a center of work and spiritual service; or rather it becomes like Mount Golgotha, enjoying the Cross of the Lord Christ planted within it, sharing with its Bridegroom His sufferings and crucifixion so as to enjoy the power of His resurrection. In short, the mountains mentioned in the Holy Bible hold memories that move the soul to enjoy, in one form or another, the life of union with God in Christ Jesus.

6.0.5.en: St. Jerome sees that these holy mountains are the prophets and the apostles, for he says: [We interpret the mountains in two ways: in the Old Testament they are the prophets, and in the New Testament the apostles. Of these mountains the Holy Bible says: “I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help” (Ps 120:1). On these mountains the city of God is established, for “a city that is set on an hill cannot be hid” (Mt 5:12). And we also, who were in darkness and the shadow of death, have been shone upon by the Lord from His eternal mountains, that is, through His prophets and apostles.]

6.0.6.en: And just as the Lord God raises His children as holy mountains in which He dwells, so the enemy of good raises from his servants defiled and stumbling mountains. If the holy mountain means the soul’s rising to the heavenly places by the Holy Spirit, then the evil mountain means the pride of the soul and its disobedience to the divine commandment. So instead of the soul being a mountain to which the Lord goes to pray (Mk 6:46), “the hill which God desireth to dwell in for ever” (Ps 68:16), it becomes defiled, a place where swine feed (Lk 8:32). And instead of the soul being that mountain to which the Church goes up with her Bridegroom as on Mount Tabor, it becomes a cause of wandering (Heb 11:38). Therefore the Lord declares His wrath against the evil mountains and shakes their foundations, or as the psalmist says: “the mountains are carried into the midst of the seas” (Ps 46:2), “What ails you, O mountains, that you skipped like rams?” (Ps 114:2). The Lord threatens these mountains, saying: “Behold, I am against thee, O destroying mountain, saith the LORD, which destroyest all the earth: and I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain. And they shall not take of thee a stone for a corner, nor a stone for foundations; but thou shalt be desolate for ever, saith the LORD” (Jer 51:25-26); as He also says: “I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the wolves of the wilderness” (Mal 1:3), “Lift ye up a banner upon the bare mountain, exalt the voice unto them” (Isa 13:2).

6.0.7.en: The people turned aside to pagan worship, so the Lord threatened them through the prophet with evil coming upon every place used for evil, whether mountain or hill, valley or river. The sword extends to the doers of evil, so that they are killed and their works are blotted out, their cities become waste and desolate, their high places are destroyed, their altars laid waste and their sun images broken (perhaps the canopies used for protection from the sun during worship, though the English translations say “the images that are worshiped”), and their bones are scattered around their altars as a sign of their defilement (2 Kgs 23:16). Thus the worshipers, the object of their worship and the place of worship itself are all shattered.

6.0.8.en: This is the prophecy that was directed against the mountains of Israel, and it is a bitter threat in order to move them to repentance. It is a prophecy standing in every generation against the arrogant soul: God destroys its high places, that is, He shatters the pride and haughtiness of its heart; He lays waste its altars, that is, He shatters its emotions which it has misused; He breaks its sun images, that is, He exposes it in the middle of the day and no longer covers for it (or perhaps by the sun images he meant the idols belonging to the worship of the sun). He casts down its slain before its idols, that is, He humbles it before those with whom it commits sin; its bones are scattered around its altar, that is, He declares its death spiritually, psychologically and bodily and the defilement of its life, so that all loathe it; He makes its dwelling a desolation, that is, He leaves its heart desolate, without satisfaction; and He blots out its works, a sign of the removal of all vitality and energy for work within it. This discipline is in fact the natural fruit of sin in the life of man: it kills him, kills his inner energies and shatters every possibility in him!

6.0.9.en: Here we notice that the Promised Land, flowing with milk and honey, which bore witness to God’s good pleasure in His believers, turns into a mass grave. Instead of bearing fruit, it becomes a place of death.

6.0.10.en: On another side, God threatens to kill them beside the altar of the demons, to prove to them its inability to help... Perhaps He wished to show them His justice: since they defiled His temple with idols, He allows the idols to be defiled by killing them in the pagan temples and turning these into graves that carry corruption.

6.1.s.en: 2. His acceptance of the repentant remnant:

6.1.0.en: 8 “Yet will I leave a remnant, that ye may have some that shall escape the sword among the nations, when ye shall be scattered through the countries. 9 And they that escape of you shall remember me among the nations whither they shall be carried captives, when I have broken their whorish heart, which hath departed from me, and their eyes, which go a whoring after their idols: and they shall lothe themselves for the evils which they have committed in all their abominations. 10 And they shall know that I am the LORD, and that I have not said in vain that I would do this evil unto them.

6.2.0.en: Each time He threatens the community or the whole people, He does not forget to stress His care for the repentant remnant who return to Him, despite their small number, those who are saved from the punishment not by accepting the discipline (the captivity) but by their repentance from their sins: “When I have broken their whorish heart, which hath departed from me, and their eyes, which go a whoring after their idols: and they shall lothe themselves for the evils which they have committed in all their abominations” [9]. They sinned like their brothers and fell into fornication, idolatry and every abomination, but they accepted the Lord’s discipline with wisdom, so that their hearts were broken by repentance and they regretted, unable to bear themselves because of what they had done. Therefore the Lord returns to them to save them, “and they shall know that I am the LORD” [10]... that is, He grants them His divine knowledge.

6.2.1.en: Truly, there is no way to our salvation except repentance, which blots out all our faults by the merits of the precious Blood through the Holy Spirit. Therefore St. Mark the Ascetic says: [God does not judge us because we have sinned, but He judges us because we have not repented.]

6.3.0.en: 11 “Thus saith the Lord GOD; Smite with thine hand, and stamp with thy foot, and say, Alas for all the evil abominations of the house of Israel! for they shall fall by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence. 12 He that is far off shall die of the pestilence; and he that is near shall fall by the sword; and he that remaineth and is besieged shall die by the famine: thus will I accomplish my fury upon them. 13 Then shall ye know that I am the LORD, when their slain men shall be among their idols round about their altars, upon every high hill, in all the tops of the mountains, and under every green tree, and under every thick oak, the place where they did offer sweet savour to all their idols. 14 So will I stretch out my hand upon them, and make the land desolate and waste, from the wilderness to Diblah, in all their habitations: and they shall know that I am the LORD.”

6.4.0.en: The Lord commanded him to clap his hand and stamp the ground with his feet like a stubborn child who has no strength or power, groaning over all their abominations, especially since the fruit of evil had begun to come upon them, killing by the sword, hunger and pestilence. It is as though the divine wrath had come upon them, so that people rose up against them, and the earth declared its anger, and all nature with it. The discipline will be more severe in the places used for pagan worship: the high hills, the tops of the mountains and under the shade of the trees, especially the oak... where they used to offer “sweet savour to all their idols” [13], which became for them the savour of death!

6.4.1.en: He declared that devastation creeps over the land from the wilderness to Diblah. Some see it as a town in the place of modern Dibl, north of Galilee, but the prevailing opinion is that it is Riblah, a city in the land of Hamath (2 Kgs 23:33; 25:20-21), as though by saying “from the wilderness to Diblah” he meant from the farthest south to the farthest north. Perhaps he also wished to declare the bitterness of what would happen to them in the person of their king: when Zedekiah was arrested after fleeing from Jerusalem, he was brought to Nebuchadnezzar, who was at Riblah, and he put out his eyes and bound him in chains to send him to Babylon (2 Kgs 25:6 etc.; Jer 39:5-7; 25:9-11).

6.4.3.en: * Wonderful are Your works, O Lord!

6.4.4.en: You have made me a mountain holy to You, I who am dust and sand!

6.4.5.en: Count me as Mount Horeb on which You declare Your Law, and as Mount Tabor on which You are transfigured in Your radiance, and as Mount Golgotha on which You offer the surpassing sacrifice of Your love!

6.4.6.en: * On the mountains Israel set up his idols like the nations, and defiled the high places with his abominations!

6.4.7.en: In Your love You discipline, bringing a sword and destroying the high places, and the cities turn into desolation!

6.4.8.en: But You do not forget the holy remnant, for You are the merciful God!

6.4.9.en: Remove from my mountains all abominations; burn with the fire of Your Holy Spirit all the thorns of sin!

6.4.10.en: Sanctify me, and count me Your holy mountain!

7.0.s.en: 1. The end is at the doors:

7.0.0.en: 1 Moreover the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 “Also, thou son of man, thus saith the Lord GOD unto the land of Israel; An end, the end is come upon the four corners of the land. 3 Now is the end come upon thee, and I will send mine anger upon thee, and will judge thee according to thy ways, and will recompense upon thee all thine abominations. 4 And mine eye shall not spare thee, neither will I have pity: but I will recompense thy ways upon thee, and thine abominations shall be in the midst of thee: and ye shall know that I am the LORD. 5 Thus saith the Lord GOD; An evil, an only evil, behold, is come. 6 An end is come, the end is come: it watcheth for thee; behold, it is come. 7 The turn is come unto thee, O thou that dwellest in the land: the time is come, the day of trouble is near, and not the sounding again of the mountains. 8 Now will I shortly pour out my fury upon thee, and accomplish mine anger upon thee: and I will judge thee according to thy ways, and will recompense thee for all thine abominations. 9 And mine eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity: I will recompense thee according to thy ways and thine abominations that are in the midst of thee; and ye shall know that I am the LORD that smiteth. 10 Behold the day, behold, it is come: the circle hath turned about; the rod hath blossomed, pride hath budded. 11 Violence is risen up into a rod of wickedness: none of them shall remain, nor of their multitude, nor of their wealth: neither shall there be wailing for them.

7.0.1.en: St. Peter the Apostle recorded for us the thinking of the scoffers who walk after their own lusts, those who say: “Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation” (2 Pet 3:4). And the Apostle Paul rebukes them: “Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance? But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God” (Rom 2:4-5).

7.0.2.en: Here the Lord affirms that the time of punishment has drawn near, which the Jewish people thought would never happen. Therefore the phrases are repeated in this chapter: “An end, the end is come, now is the end come upon thee (against thee), an evil is come, the time is come, the day is come” [2, 5, 6, 12]. And he spoke of the end from three sides:

7.0.3.en: a. The end is extremely painful [1-6].

7.1.0.en: b. The end is at the doors [7-10].

7.1.1.en: c. The end is inevitable, with no escape [10-15].

7.1.2.en: The end came when their consciences became utterly hardened and there was no longer in their lives the least sign of repentance. Therefore God judges them according to their evil ways and abominations, because they did not listen to His prophets, nor did they repent of their idolatry.

7.1.3.en: The end is extremely painful, not because God wants the bitterness of their souls, for He still loves them, but because this is the nature of sin itself, its nature being turmoil and distress, for He says: “the day of trouble is near, and not the sounding again of the mountains” [7]. The songs of praise ended, joy was taken from them, and anxiety and distress came with the coming of sin into their lives. This is what He affirms by saying: “I will recompense thy ways upon thee, and thine abominations shall be in the midst of thee” [4]. It is as though the Lord affirms that what befalls her is the very nature of the corruption of sin and the abominations which man has chosen for himself, for it carries its punishment within itself.

7.1.4.en: This is what St. Augustine affirms as he comments on the words of the psalmist: [“As wax melteth, so let the wicked perish”] (Ps 68:2): [They perish by a kind of fire of their lusts. Here (in the world) there is a kind of hidden punishment of sinners of which the psalm speaks... For evil lust is like burning and fire. Does fire burn a garment while the lust of fornication does not burn the soul?! For the Scripture says of deliberate fornication: “Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burned?” (Prov 6:27)... And the Apostle says: “Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts” (Rom 1:24). See the fire that makes him melt like wax!]

7.1.5.en: “The turn is come unto thee, O thou that dwellest in the land” [7]. Since the heart of the wicked dwells on the earth and becomes dust, his turn comes with the turning of the wheel of divine judgment, and there is none who can turn it from its course... The day of wrath comes. But whoever lifts his heart by repentance to heaven does not fall under wrath but enjoys the divine mercy.

7.2.0.en: When the wicked who persist in their evil fall under wrath, they do not see the Lord the Shepherd but “the LORD that smiteth,” for He says: “and ye shall know that I am the LORD that smiteth” [9].

7.2.1.en: When the Lord declares the nearness of the painful end, which is the natural fruit of uncleannesses, He makes clear what the uncleannesses are so that believers may turn back from them.

7.3.0.en: a. Pride: “the rod hath blossomed, pride hath budded” [10]. For the people’s fall into pagan worship or fornication was caused by pride. This is the beginning of the pains of the soul, which shattered the devil and brought him down from the highest heavenly ranks to the abyss, and which drove Adam and Eve out of Paradise. Therefore God humbles the proud, not because He desires to humble them, but in order to cut off from them what belongs to Satan, so that they may, in the spirit of humility, repent, submitting to the divine commandment.

7.4.0.en: b. Violence: “Violence is risen up into a rod of wickedness” [11]. If pride touches chiefly man’s relationship with God, violence touches man’s relationship with his brother, and though the two are linked together, both are indicators of hardness of heart as an evil nature that corrupts man’s inner life and consequently his dealings with God and man.

7.4.1.en: Pride drives man to humiliation with none to be gentle with him, and violence drives him to the loss of what he has with none to have mercy on him: “none of them shall remain, nor of their multitude, nor of their wealth: neither shall there be wailing for them” [11].

7.5.0.en: 12 “The time is come, the day draweth near: let not the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn: for wrath is upon all the multitude thereof. 13 For the seller shall not return to that which is sold, although they were yet alive: for the vision is touching the whole multitude thereof, which shall not return; neither shall any strengthen himself in the iniquity of his life. 14 They have blown the trumpet, even to make all ready; but none goeth to the battle: for my wrath is upon all the multitude thereof. 15 The sword is without, and the pestilence and the famine within: he that is in the field shall die with the sword; and he that is in the city, famine and pestilence shall devour him. 16 But they that escape of them shall escape, and shall be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them mourning, every one for his iniquity. 17 All hands shall be feeble, and all knees shall be weak as water. 18 They shall also gird themselves with sackcloth, and horror shall cover them; and shame shall be upon all faces, and baldness upon all their heads. 19 They shall cast their silver in the streets, and their gold shall be an unclean thing: their silver and their gold shall not be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of the LORD: they shall not satisfy their souls, neither fill their bowels: because it is the stumblingblock of their iniquity.

7.6.0.en: If our temporal life distracts us from spiritual preparation to meet the Lord, God sometimes allows us distress in all aspects of our temporal life, perhaps so that we may return and think about God’s threats and chastisements. Therefore He speaks to them here of a state of ruin and complete destruction of the city socially and economically: the buyer does not rejoice because he has nothing to buy with, nor the seller because he will not return to his trade; the trumpets are blown for war, but there is no man who rises to fight... a state of total loss! The sword pursues them from without, and pestilence and famine from within, and those who flee are not like strong lions but in the weakness of the doves that fly with constant moaning; they mourn as they see the city utterly ruined. They lose all bodily, psychological and spiritual energy: “All hands shall be feeble, and all knees shall be weak as water.” They enter a state of intense grief like one mourning a dead man, for “they shall also gird themselves with sackcloth... and baldness upon all their heads” [18].

7.6.1.en: Horror takes hold of them, and their silver and their gold which they had stored up cannot deliver them in the day of the divine wrath. They have lost all their hope, all their strength and all their holiness!

7.7.0.en: Their wealth, which distracted them from attention to the divine commandments and heavenly threats, cannot save them but becomes the cause of their destruction, since they use it in the worship of idols: “They shall cast their silver in the streets, and their gold shall be an unclean thing” [19]. What is silver but the word of God, purified seven times? Instead of keeping it in their hearts and preserving it in their inner storehouses, they cast it into the streets and neglect it. As for gold, which signifies the heavenly things, instead of lifting their lives to fellowship with God so as to experience the heavenly life within them, they stumble over heavenly things and grow in uncleanness!

7.8.s.en: 3. The end of formal religious life:

7.8.0.en: 20 “As for the beauty of his ornament, he set it in majesty: but they made the images of their abominations and of their detestable things therein: therefore have I made it unto them an unclean thing. 21 And I will give it into the hands of the strangers for a prey, and to the wicked of the earth for a spoil; and they shall pollute it. 22 My face will I turn also from them, and they shall pollute my secret place: for the robbers shall enter into it, and defile it. 23 Make a chain: for the land is full of bloody crimes, and the city is full of violence. 24 Wherefore I will bring the worst of the heathen, and they shall possess their houses: I will also make the pomp of the strong to cease; and their holy places shall be defiled. 25 Destruction cometh; and they shall seek peace, and there shall be none. 26 Mischief shall come upon mischief, and rumour shall be upon rumour; then shall they seek a vision of the prophet; but the law shall perish from the priest, and counsel from the ancients.

7.8.1.en: If the former left God because of love of the world, and therefore God allowed the ruin of the city and all that is in it, others were occupied away from God through the formalities of worship, and therefore God allowed the ruin of the visible temple, perhaps that they might care for the inner temple in the heart.

7.8.2.en: God delivered their cities and their land to be plundered by foreign hands, and behold, He delivers His temple also to strangers.

7.9.0.en: His people defiled His altar with the worship of idols, so the Lord delivered His temple to the foreign soldiers who besieged it, to plunder it, and to the wicked of the earth to spoil it. He turned His face from His house since His children had turned it into a den of robbers, leaving the wicked to do what is not fitting: “My face will I turn also from them, and they shall pollute my secret place: for the robbers shall enter into it, and defile it” [22].

7.10.0.en: The defilement of the altar does not stop at their accepting pagan worship, but extends to their breaking the divine commandment and walking in injustice. Therefore God counts their worship a defilement of His temple, since it comes from a heart stained with blood and full of injustice. They defiled His temple, so He lets strangers defile their holy places, perhaps meaning the temple itself or their houses as sanctuaries. He says: “Make a chain: for the land is full of bloody crimes, and the city is full of violence. Wherefore I will bring the worst of the heathen, and they shall possess their houses: I will also make the pomp of the strong to cease; and their holy places shall be defiled” [23-24]. He allows the preparing of the chain, that is, the fetters for their captivity, for they had bound themselves with the chains of their sins; therefore they are delivered into the hands of the enemies, bound with visible chains of metal. Perhaps He also prepared the chain of His divine justice to punish them!

7.10.1.en: Besides their worship of idols and their breaking of the commandment, they resort to deceiving themselves with false prophecies. Instead of repentance they ask the prophets and priests for a false and deceptive peace. Therefore false prophets appeared who prophesy not according to God’s command but according to what pleases the desires of the people, and the law perished from the priest and counsel from the ancients... These say “Peace, peace; when there is no peace” (Jer 8:11).

7.10.2.en: Let every believer beware, and every family, and also every church, for if something forbidden enters, ruin comes and all fall under the wrath of God! And it is said, “There is an accursed thing in the midst of thee, O Israel” (Josh 7:13).

7.11.s.en: 4. The end of the temporal kingship:

7.11.0.en: 27 “The king shall mourn, and the prince shall be clothed with desolation, and the hands of the people of the land shall be troubled: I will do unto them after their way, and according to their deserts will I judge them; and they shall know that I am the LORD.”

7.11.1.en: “The king shall mourn, and the prince shall be clothed with desolation, and the hands of the people of the land shall be troubled” [27]. Thus man sometimes relies on temporal authority, thinking that the Lord’s chastisements will not touch him; therefore the Lord breaks this temporal authority, and the king mourns... Here he refers to Jehoiachin (Ezek 27:12) and the former kings (Ezek 43:7, 9), as well as to the kings who will rule in the future (Ezek 37:22, 24), but he does not mean King Zedekiah (Ezek 12:12; 21:25). As for the prince (Prince), he means the head of the new community, or the ruling class at that time. As for the people of the land, before the captivity this referred to non-Hebrews (Ezra 4:4; Neh 10:31), but here he means the Jewish people.

7.11.2.en: How long will you wait, O my soul?!

7.11.3.en: * Your voice, O my God, has never ceased!

7.11.4.en: It warns me: the end is at the doors!

7.11.5.en: You are the Architect of the whole world; You know its secrets; You assure me: heaven and earth shall pass away, and I in my folly grow slack and am humiliated!

7.11.6.en: * How long will you wait, O my soul?!

7.11.7.en: Will you flee to the mountains?! Behold, they are shaken!

7.11.8.en: Will you rely on your friends?!

7.11.9.en: Behold, all hands are feeble, and all knees become like water!

7.11.10.en: Will you trust in your gold and your silver?

7.11.12.en: Will you depend on the formalities and the letter of worship!

7.11.13.en: Your God asks for the heart and the depths!

7.11.16.en: How long will you wait, O my soul?!
